//ignoreCommand: Exit 1 builds, exit 0 skips. This project is attached to the same repository as production, so without this it would also build `main` and ship the production configuration under a demo hostname. Only the demo branch builds here.
ignoreCommand: if [ "$VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_REF" = "demo" ]; then exit 1; else exit 0; fi
//rewrites: Hash routing already resolves every route to index.html; this only catches a hand-typed path. Vercel checks the filesystem before rewrites, so js/ and styles/ are unaffected.

headers.//: The app ships unbundled ES modules at stable URLs, so a browser that caches views/index.js keeps running an old build after a deploy — and a version query on the entry point cannot reach modules it imports by fixed path. Revalidation is the fix: these files are tiny and a 304 costs almost nothing.

connect-src 'self' is the load-bearing line, and the difference from production. This build has no database client and no credentials, but the policy makes that structural rather than a promise: the browser refuses any request to Supabase, to Google, or to any other host, whatever the JavaScript asks for. form-action 'none' because the build contains no form; noindex because a fixed sample should not rank above the real thing.

headers.value: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' https://fonts.googleapis.com; font-src https://fonts.gstatic.com; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'none'
